note: Plain-language due-diligence on every supplier — the ones in a recommendation and your current suppliers. Serious flags were verified against primary sources (FDA, CCI, courts). Each is a lead to verify before acting, not a final legal conclusion. Full sourced detail: research/supplier-due-diligence.md.

gujarat-ambuja-exports.headline: India's #1 maize maker — rock-solid, but profit swings with corn prices.
gujarat-ambuja-exports.verdict: Push the price — they're debt-free with spare capacity, so they can give. Don't switch; 'we'll move some to Sayaji' is your lever.
findings: Biggest maize maker in India. ~5,000 TPD, growing to 6,000, only ~82% full — lots of spare capacity.
Debt-free, AA– rated, ~₹950 cr cash. No supply risk.
Has a plant ~100 km from your Nashik/Aurangabad — easy delivery.
Profit swings with corn prices (one quarter −45%, then up). Normal, not a worry.
One blemish: a 2018 pollution closure (since lifted).

sukhjit-corn-products.headline: Healthy, well-run dextrose maker with blue-chip clients.
sukhjit-corn-products.verdict: Cut the price AND stop paying early. Both are safe to reclaim.
findings: A-rated, low debt. Clients: Dabur, Nestlé, Mars, Marico.
1,600 TPD across 4 plants — one in Himachal (near Baddi); a new ₹500 cr Nashik plant is planned, next to your Nashik site.
A margin dip cut it A+ → A. Balance sheet still strong.
Runs its bank limits ~93% full — so your early payment is cash they value.

sayaji-industries.headline: A cheaper dextrose option — but one small, shaky plant.
sayaji-industries.verdict: Use as a cheaper second source for a small, capped share. Keep the bulk with Gujarat Ambuja.

flag.label: One small plant, money's tight (recovering)
flag.detail: One 950 TPD plant (Ahmedabad), no expansion planned — so it can take some extra, not a lot. Below investment grade (BB+), kept going by promoter loans + a ₹73 cr land sale. Now recovering — back to a thin profit, outlook up to Positive (Sep 2026).

findings: Move some here for the lower price — but not a big block.
Why not all: one plant, no expansion, and shaky finances (BB+).
FY26 is a real but thin turnaround — watch it prove out.
Pharma grade not confirmed — get the IP-grade COA + certs first.

universal-starch-chem-allied.headline: Small, secretive dextrose maker that went dark on its rating agency.
universal-starch-chem-allied.verdict: Push the price; don't lean on them. The secrecy is the flag.
findings: Stopped sharing its books with the rating agency — downgraded to BB for it.
One ~500 TPD plant at Dhule — closest dextrose maker to your Nashik/Aurangabad (~100 km), but tiny and opaque.
Got into dextrose by buying a bank-auctioned distressed plant for ₹17 cr.
Small (~₹490 cr sales), no dividends, high-pollution plant.

geep-industries-india.headline: Your biggest laminate supplier — and a convicted cartel member.
geep-industries-india.verdict: Push the price hard; don't grow reliance. The conviction and thin focus are real flags.

flag.label: Convicted of price-fixing (CCI, 2018)
flag.detail: India's competition regulator found GEEP guilty in 2018 of a price-fixing cartel (with Panasonic, in batteries); upheld on appeal. 'GEEP' is really the old battery/torch brand — laminate is a side business.

findings: A battery/torch/LED firm that also makes laminate — packaging isn't its focus.
Doesn't publish its laminate capacity; tiny rated bank lines (₹25 cr) — no sign of scale to grow into.
Margins fell from ~8.6% to ~3%; low debt, but its growth is LED/EV, not laminate.
Has a Baddi unit next to your Baddi plant (handy), but no pharma-grade proof.

shrinath-roto-pack.headline: A real, pharma-grade laminate option — but carrying factory debt.
shrinath-roto-pack.verdict: Bring in as a second source beside GEEP — capped, after a cert + capacity audit. Don't hand them everything.
findings: Why consider it: 57,540 t/yr (2 Hyderabad plants), BBB+ (stronger than GEEP), real clients (GSK, P&G, Britannia).
The catch: its foil plant is debt-funded, only ~40–50% used, and drags the group's credit. No new capex planned.
Foil plant is near your Waluj (Aurangabad), but the laminate is made far away in Hyderabad — a freight cost.
Pharma grade claimed, not proven — audit the certs + spare capacity first.

tetrapak-india.headline: Rock-solid global supplier — you're just paying them too early.
tetrapak-india.verdict: Stop paying early; push for 30-day credit. They have no basis to make you pay upfront.
findings: A dominant MNC; India's biggest Tetra Pak plant is near Pune.
They finance their own customers (credit + leasing) — so no reason you should pay upfront.
The group has two of the biggest antitrust fines ever (EU + China), for tying cartons to machines.

gls-films-industries-p.headline: Plenty of laminate capacity — but shaky finances and a fatal fire.
gls-films-industries-p.verdict: Push the price hard; don't lean on them more without fresh financial + safety comfort.

flag.label: Nearly went insolvent, plus a deadly fire at the group
flag.detail: A creditor got GLS into insolvency court (2025); the Supreme Court reversed it (2026). The group didn't cover its interest in FY24 and shows 'rating shopping'. Separately, a reactor blast at sister firm GLS Speciality Chemicals killed 4 workers (May 2026); the safety officer was arrested.

findings: Has spare capacity (~50% used) and good clients (ITC, PepsiCo, Nestlé) — capacity isn't the worry.
The group didn't cover its interest in FY24 (0.86x), heavily geared.
Flagship sales fell ~23%; survives on promoter loans and cross-guarantees.

huhtamaki-india.headline: Very strong, pharma-grade laminate maker — the safe alternative.
huhtamaki-india.verdict: Safe to move volume here and use their flat sales to push price. Watch the leadership change.
findings: Very safe (AA–), almost no debt, >₹400 cr cash, Finnish parent — can easily take volume.
Pharma-grade; ~10 plants incl. Himachal (near Baddi) and Maharashtra (near you).
The trade-off: premium pricing, higher than Roto Pack — a quality benchmark, not the cheap option.
Watch: the MD and CFO both quit within ~3 months (late 2025).

uflex.headline: India's biggest flexible-packaging firm — capable, but debt + governance flags.
uflex.verdict: Use as a price benchmark only; don't concentrate volume. The chairman's conviction + debt are the flags.

flag.label: Chairman convicted in a corruption case
flag.detail: Founder-chairman Ashok Chaturvedi was convicted (2010 Noida land scam) and jailed. The company is also heavily indebted (net-debt/EBITDA 4.25x, outlook cut to Negative). Note: a 2023 tax-raid headline collapsed at the tax tribunal in 2026.

findings: Big and capable — a good price benchmark for other laminate suppliers.
Heavily indebted; outlook cut to Negative; thin ~2% margins.
Trades at ~0.4x book — the market discounts it heavily.

silk-polypack.headline: Not really a supplier — a single one-off buy.
silk-polypack.verdict: Drop it from your alternatives (confirming with you — nothing removed on our own).
findings: One purchase ever in your records — ₹7,775, 31 kg of laminate (Mar 2026).
No company registry or web presence, because there's nothing there.

chemco-plastic-industries.headline: Strong, pharma-grade bottle maker — 'old stock' is just how they run.
chemco-plastic-industries.verdict: Keep them — just add a 'freshest-first / max-age-at-dispatch' clause for ORS shelf life.
findings: Strong (A+), ~₹939 cr sales, pharma clients (Cipla, J&J). India's biggest PET-preform maker — lots of capacity, still expanding.
The 'old stock' is their deliberate ~125-day inventory model (confirmed), not distress.
Plants in the Gujarat/Silvassa belt (~180–220 km from Nashik).

cincorp-international.headline: A real bottle maker — but you can't find it in any public record.
cincorp-international.verdict: Use the overpay data to negotiate; confirm the exact entity from a GST invoice before leaning on them.
findings: Your records show 121 deliveries of bottles + caps to Baddi — so it's real.
But a deep search found NO public record for 'Cincorp International' at all — you can't confirm the legal entity from outside your ledger.
Pin the exact invoicing entity (GST) and audit before any volume move.

pik-plastics.headline: A real but tiny Surat bottle maker — unaudited.
pik-plastics.verdict: Fine for price leverage; don't move volume without an on-site audit + documents.
findings: A real one-owner firm (Surat) with a Vapi factory + a Haridwar branch.
No audited accounts, capacity or pharma certs could be checked.

premier-plastic.headline: A tiny one-owner plastics shop — weakest pharma fit.
premier-plastic.verdict: Confirm which 'Premier' invoices you (GST), then audit before any volume move.
findings: The real supplier is a tiny Vasai proprietorship — NOT the listed 'Premier Polyfilm' (that's flooring).
Vasai is ~130 km from Nashik and near Mumbai/Goa — best-located of the tiny makers.
But its range is general plastics (jars, tubes, even scarf hangers) — thin pharma-bottle proof.

mars-plastics.headline: A small Punjab firm — best product fit of the tiny bottle makers.
mars-plastics.verdict: Use the low price as leverage; audit (GMP + certs + capacity) before moving these light-sensitive bottles.
findings: Why it tempts: makes exactly the right bottles (dry-syrup, eye-drop, nasal) at the lowest price, and Samana is ~180 km from Baddi — closest of the small makers.
Why to audit first: a small partnership, no audited accounts, no confirmed certs (ISO 15378/GMP) — a cheap price can mean thinner walls or looser QC.

berry-global-india.headline: Backed by a global giant (Amcor) — but check they make your bottle.
berry-global-india.verdict: Safe on parent strength — first confirm the India plant makes your exact ORS bottle.
findings: Parent is now Amcor (~$13bn, investment-grade) — rock-solid.
But the India arm is tiny and loss-making, and its Bangalore site makes droppers/inhalers — maybe not plain bottles. Bangalore is also far from your plants.
Amcor is mid-restructuring (US plant closures so far).

suraj-blow-plast.headline: A real small bottle maker — just no public footprint.
suraj-blow-plast.verdict: Use as leverage; get the legal entity (GST) and audit before bigger volume.
findings: Your records show 38 deliveries of amber PET bottles to Aurangabad (~₹4.95/pc) — likely local to your Waluj plant (a logistics plus).
No public registry/web at all — no financials, capacity or certs to check.
Amber PET suits light-sensitive products, but unproven UV/QC is where a cheap maker can slip.

tpac-packaging-india.headline: Healthy, A-rated bottle maker backed by a Thai group.
tpac-packaging-india.verdict: Push the price (ideally a resin-cost-linked clause). Safe to keep or grow.
findings: A-rated (ICRA, Mar 2026), ~₹822 cr sales, pharma-capable; just added capacity, so room to grow.
Plants at Umbergaon/Silvassa ~150 km from Nashik — good logistics.
Watch: profit dipped ~31% last year, and it leans ~85–90% on one supplier of its own.

kilitch-healthcare-india.headline: Flagged for old stock — and the most serious finding of the lot.
kilitch-healthcare-india.verdict: Treat as high risk. Demand their FDA fix-it evidence and re-qualify them, or move the business.

flag.label: US FDA found faked lab data + an import ban
flag.detail: FDA Warning Letter (Mar 2024): it's their 'routine practice to fabricate results for samples never taken', plus unsanitary conditions. On FDA Import Alert since Oct 2023; the maker behind the 2023 US eye-drop recall. Faked QC data means you can't trust any of their test paperwork. (This is the unlisted Kilitch Healthcare, not the clean listed Kilitch Drugs.)

findings: A pharma contract-maker — likely supplies you filled goods, not empty bottles.
Formerly 'NBZ Pharma'; FY25 profit fell ~44% after the import ban.
Their ~211-day-old stock is doubly worrying given the faked-data findings.

empire-industries-virum-glass.headline: Your amber glass-bottle maker — a steady niche unit of a cash-rich group.
empire-industries-virum-glass.verdict: Keep — a steady, low-risk amber-bottle maker. Just confirm the glass type (Type I vs III) suits you.
findings: Cash-rich, low-debt group (its real profit engine is property rentals); glass sales ~₹246 cr.
One Vikhroli plant (~1.9 million bottles/day), ~165 km from Nashik — but one furnace, so limited room for a big surge.
Glass is a small, non-core unit; thin disclosure, no standalone rating.

bprex-pharma-packaging-india-p.headline: A cGMP pharma-packaging maker built for eye-drops — now part of Amcor.
bprex-pharma-packaging-india-p.verdict: Keep — a low-risk MNC vendor. Confirm which entity (Bprex vs Berry) actually invoices you.
findings: Strong lineage: Truepack → Rexam → Berry → Amcor (2025); investment-grade parent.
Bangalore cGMP clean-room makes dropper bottles — a strong fit for your eye-drops.
Same Bangalore address + directors as Berry Global India (same Amcor group).

pgp-glass.headline: A world-scale glass leader (ex-Piramal) — very capable, but changing owners.
pgp-glass.verdict: Keep; watch the Blackstone IPO/sale — an owner change could shift focus off domestic pharma.

flag.label: Owner in flux
flag.detail: 100% owned by Blackstone (since 2020), now running both an IPO (~$4bn aim) and sale talks (Brookfield ~$1.3–1.5bn), plus a ₹2,597 cr loan due Mar 2026 being refinanced. Pharma is only ~21% of its sales, so an owner change could pull focus off your low-margin pharma glass.

findings: Very capable: 1,730 TPD (new Kosamba furnace), A+ rated, ~₹4,216 cr sales — lots of capacity.
But pharma is only ~21% of its book — mostly luxury cosmetics + spirits bottles.
Strong ESG record; zero fatalities FY25.

sources.label: CARE, Dec 2025; PGP FY25 annual report

rachana-plastics.headline: A one-man Mumbai maker of caps + measuring cups — clean, but tiny and opaque.
rachana-plastics.verdict: Low-stakes caps/cups supplier. Pin the GST entity and check food-grade (FSSAI) compliance.
findings: Almost certainly a one-owner firm (Jignesh Gandhi) — key-person risk.
Makes flip-off seals, screw/child-resistant caps, 5/15/250 ml cups — ORS-relevant.
No public financials; clean record, but no transparency.

abhinav-speciality-foods-llp.headline: A tiny, opaque Mumbai family LLP — unclear what it even supplies you.
abhinav-speciality-foods-llp.verdict: Get its FSSAI licence, the exact product spec/COA + GST, and clarify the Ayurvedic link.
findings: Very small (~₹4 cr sales) and heavily in debt.
Office in Andheri, no visible factory; the exact ingredient isn't findable publicly.
Sits next to an Ayurvedic business (Abhinav Healthcare) — highest info-risk of the set.

triveni-polymers.headline: The standout small vendor — it's Gerresheimer's India arm (a German MNC).
triveni-polymers.verdict: Your strongest small vendor — a tier-1 global player. Keep, and you could safely grow it.
findings: Gerresheimer-controlled (took 75% in 2012; exact current stake not public). Branded 'Gerresheimer Kundli'.
USFDA-DMF-certified (first Indian firm for plastic pharma containers); ISO 9001/14001/15378/45001 — the most certified plastic maker you use.
Clean-room plants at Kundli (~230 km from Baddi) + Kosamba. No public capacity figure — confirm headroom first.

scorpion-containers.headline: Named like a packaging maker — but it looks like a freight/logistics firm.
scorpion-containers.verdict: Confirm what they actually supply you (bottles vs transport) before treating them as a packaging vendor.

flag.label: May not be a packaging maker at all
flag.detail: Despite the 'Containers' name, the trail (courier GST codes, 10+ multi-state registrations, the 'Scorpion Express' 3PL logistics group) points to freight, not manufacturing. Only one thin packaging listing exists. Your relationship with them may be transport, not bottles.

findings: Tiny (paid-up under ₹1 cr); no rating, no financials, no verifiable plant.
Run by the Singh family, who also run the Scorpion Express logistics group.
The 'packaging supplier' idea is only weakly supported.
